newsitem.title: USA: Former presidents urge campaign finance reform.
newsitem.headline: Former presidents urge campaign finance reform.

text.p: Former Presidents Gerald Ford, Jimmy Carter and George Bush added their voices to the chorus urging Congress and the White House to enact campaign finance reform legislation in letters released Thursday.

The former presidents called for a ban on so-called "soft money" donations to political parties by corporations and unions, improved disclosure of campaign spending and fund-raising, and better enforcement of campaign finance laws.

The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee earlier this month began well-publicised hearings on how foreign money was illegally raised and spent in the 1996 elections and whether U.S. security was compromised by individuals who may have shared secret information with foreign business interests.

The matter is also being probed by Justice Department, but Attorney General Janet Reno has resisted repeated calls by Republicans to recommend appointment of a special prosecutor to conduct an independent investigation.

The letters by Ford, Carter and Bush were released by former Sen. Nancy Kassebaum Baker and former Vice President Walter Mondale, who are spearheading a presidential bipartisan effort on campaign finance reform that kicked off last month.

The "future of our democracy" requires "prompt and fundamental repair of our system for financing federal elections," Carter said in a letter to Mondale and Kassebaum. "We must take significant steps to assure voters that public policy is determined by the exercise of their franchise rather than a broken and suspect campaign finance system."
In his letter, Bush said any campaign fund-raising reform enacted should "go the extra mile in demanding fullest possible disclosure of all campaign contributions."
Kassebaum Baker and Mondale said the letters underscored the "desire of the American people for meaningful, bipartisan reform."
